📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-06-synthetics-signin-transient-step-duration-spike`
This is occurrence #10 (6+ weeks since first seen).
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Admin` (`@admin` / `#team-admin`)
Playbook: Confirm shape via avg:synthetics.browser.step.duration{step_id IN (...)} — expect a single/double-run breach just over 20s, self-recovering next run; check for co-firing critical-path monitors (gateway/oauth2/ms-authentication-api/ms-identity-api) before assuming noise.
Open Jira: none

Source alerts (1 total):
  • https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/127198928

Evidence:
  • DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/127198928 — "[Synthetics] Sign in to Method" (OK, last_triggered 2026-07-08T23:33:08Z)
  • DD metric: https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&exp_metric=synthetics.browser.step.duration&exp_scope=check_type%3Abrowser&start=1783632900&end=1783634700 — 2 breach points this cycle: 20527ms@23:21:10Z, 20084ms@23:30:00Z (2-7% over the 20s threshold), falling back to 4.8-7.6s on adjacent runs
  • This-window concentration: no co-firing critical-path monitor (gateway/oauth2/ms-authentication-api/ms-identity-api all quiet)

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-05-rainforest-outbound-api-p95-latency`
This is occurrence #6 since 2026-07-05.
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Transactions` (`@transactions` / `#team-transactions`)
Playbook: Third-party (Rainforest payment processor) outbound latency — no Method-side code fix. Re-run the p95 metric over a widened window (data is sparse); confirm 0 errors on service:runtime-core-api; escalate to Ben only if errors start appearing or frequency increases sharply.
Open Jira: none

Source alerts (1 total):
  • https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/295928665

Evidence:
  • DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/295928665 — "[Rainforest] Outbound API P95 Latency > 3s" (OK, last_triggered 2026-07-09T08:21:26Z)
  • DD metric: https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&exp_metric=trace.http.request&exp_scope=peer.hostname%3Aapi.rainforestpay.com&exp_agg=p95&start=1783576800&end=1783580200 — 30 points 08:00-08:50Z, range 0.25-2.66s (sparse, did not reproduce the exact trigger-window peak, consistent with prior occurrences)
  • This-window concentration: 0 hits on service:runtime-core-api status:error (latency-only, third-party dependency)
  • Note: this monitor's real Slack channel is #alert-transactions, which is not in kb/config.json.channels — only caught via this cycle's full DD monitor scan (documented gap, see memory project_alert_transactions_gap)

🚨 *new alert — needs human*  (score: 8)
Channel: alert-system  •  bug-type guess: unknown (latency, no errors)  •  alerts in group: 1
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Admin` (`@admin` / `#team-admin`)

Symptoms:
  - ms-authentication-api (critical-path auth service) p95 latency sustained ~1h elevation, 08:52-09:48Z
  - 34 of 180 sampled points (19%) exceeded the 0.5s monitor threshold; peak 1.77s at 09:48:00Z (3.5x raw / 2.55x-over-threshold ratio)
  - Zero application errors in the window (latency-only, not an error cascade)
  - Explicitly checked and ruled OUT correlation with the same-morning "Redis Errors is High" monitor (fired 10:09:35Z) — Redis errors were flat near-zero throughout this latency window and only spiked ~15min after this episode had already ended

Trace IDs: none captured (APM trace search not wired into current tooling; DD APM traces link below for manual drill-down)
Likely cause: unidentified — no error signal, no Redis correlation, deploy correlation blocked (methodcrm-org GH_TOKEN 403 gap, ms-authentication-api local clone stale since 2026-04-30)
Suggested next action: monitor — if this recurs, escalate to Admin team to check ms-authentication-api's SQL/Mongo dependency latency and host-level resource contention during the spike window

Source alerts (1 total):
  • https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/299551532 (alert-system, 09:27 UTC)

Evidence:
  • DD monitors: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/299551532 — "[Admin][AuthenticationAPI][P2] P95 latency high (ms-authentication-api)" (OK by scan time, last_triggered 2026-07-09T09:27:32Z)
  • DD metrics: https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&exp_metric=trace.aspnet_core.request&exp_scope=service%3Ams-authentication-api%2Cenv%3Aprod&exp_agg=p95&start=1783587000&end=1783590600
  • DD APM traces: https://app.datadoghq.com/apm/traces?query=service%3Ams-authentication-api%20%40duration%3A%3E0.5s&start=1783587000000&end=1783590600000
  • Kibana: URL unavailable (set KIBANA_BASE_URL in .env) — not queried this finding (evidence_source is datadog_apm, latency-only per playbook)
  • New KB entry written this cycle: ki-2026-07-09-ms-authentication-api-p95-latency-sustained-noerrors — full diagnosis and playbook captured for recurrence tracking

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-06-runtime-core-redis-cache-timeout-transient-burst`
This is occurrence #6 since 2026-07-05.
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Vertical App Experience` (`@sales management` / `#team-sales-management`)
Playbook: Confirm monitor 227940275 not co-firing with RTC p95/tables-fields circuit-breaker/gateway-XHR (none did this occurrence); query trace.redis.command.errors by service; corroborate via ES messageTemplate "Redis operation timed out after 5 seconds"; compare vs before/after window for a real ratio.
Open Jira: none

Source alerts (1 total):
  • https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/227940275

Evidence:
  • DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/227940275 — "Redis Errors is High" (OK, last_triggered 2026-07-09T10:09:35Z)
  • DD metric: brief real burst confirmed — 9+4=13 errors in a single ~10s window (10:03:10-10:03:20Z), self-recovered
  • Kibana: ES messageTemplate:"Redis operation timed out after 5 seconds" AND fields.dd_service.keyword:runtime-core-api, 09:50-10:25Z — 1 hit (account "changeit")
  • This-window concentration: runtime-core-api only; no co-firing critical-path monitor. Checked and ruled OUT as the same event as this cycle's ms-authentication-api P95 latency finding (monitor 299551532, 09:27:32Z) — Redis errors were flat near-zero throughout that separate episode's window
